guide.title: Which rate limit you just hit
guide.subtitle: A plan limit and an edge limit look almost identical
guide.excerpt: There are two throttles in front of a send: the one your plan sets, and a much higher one at the network edge. Both answer with the same status code, so the message text is what tells them apart.

p: The plan limit is a product limit: it varies by subscription tier and is the number you can reason about and budget against. The edge limit sits in front of everything and exists only to keep anomalous traffic away from the service — it is set far above any plan ceiling, so a well-behaved integration should never see it.

Both return the same throttling status, and both carry the same business code. What differs is the message text: the edge limit identifies itself with a distinct prefix. Without that distinction you cannot tell "you are sending faster than your plan allows" from "something upstream flagged this traffic", and the two call for different responses.

sections.h: Retrying is not the same as fixing
list: Throttling is a pacing signal, not a failed message. Backing off and retrying is correct behavior.
Retrying faster never helps: the limit is enforced on a one-second fixed window, so a burst inside the same window simply fails again.
Sending, bulk sending, scheduled sending and the API all draw on the same allowance — they are not separate buckets.
